# Changelog — Utility bill manager

## 0.11.0

- Add a bill to Shared expenses: with the two apps connected, the owner puts the bill into an expense group with everyone’s exact share, paid by them, and opens it from there. Adding it twice changes nothing.

## 0.10.0

- Calendar: the month view shows the due dates; click a day to list the bills due then. In the year view, click a month to list its bills below. Click again, or change the view, to see everything.

## 0.9.0

- Filter events from connected apps by month or by a selected day in the Calendar tab.

## 0.8.0

- **Search for available utility services**: share your location once (or use your profile address) and get the usual services for your country and county or state with the likely provider, ready to add in one step. Suggestions for Romania, Germany and Hungary so far.
- Deleting, clearing and leaving now ask in the app’s own window, and a link that cannot be copied is shown to select.

## 0.7.1

- When a member removes their DevQuake account, what they added to your things (comments, items, ticks, photos…) stays, shown as “REMOVED_…” instead of their name.

## 0.7.0

- Pictures load faster: lists and previews show small versions, and tapping a picture opens it in full size.
- “Back” links now return to the page you came from, with its filters and where you had scrolled to.

## 0.6.0

- The app’s card on DevQuake and its front page now show how many members use it and its totals: bills, meter readings.

0.5.0

- Works with the family planner, Shared shopping lists and the workout tracker: connect them on DevQuake (“Works with” at the bottom of the page) and disconnect them there any time.
- Calendars across apps: under the calendar, “From your other apps” lists the next 31 days of the apps you connected — family events (shared ones included), shopping days and training sessions — each opening in its app. Connected apps can show the due dates of your unpaid bills (the utility’s name only, no amounts).

## 0.4.1

- People who do not use the app yet now see what it does on its front page, with a link to the user manual, and shared links show the app’s own picture.

## 0.4.0

- Add the app to your home screen: on phones and tablets, the new button in the toolbar puts the app’s icon (its logo with the DevQuake badge) on your home screen, so it opens like an app.

## 0.3.0

- Meter photos: take one with the camera or choose one from your photo library.
- View-only members: the manager can let a family member see every bill without having a share or paying.
- Confirmed payments are locked, and the person who paid gets an email with the whole bill, their consumption and share, and a link to the bill and its PDF.
- A tidier toolbar on every screen: the app’s name (tap it for the start page), full screen and the DevQuake mark. The manual and version notes moved to the bottom of the page; your language and theme are set in your DevQuake account.

## 0.2.0

- Your address is now asked in parts (country, state or county, city, street, number and an optional apartment), with suggestions from OpenStreetMap as you type. If you saved an address before, you are asked to complete it once.

## 0.1.0

- Add your utilities (electricity, gas, water, heating, phone, cable TV, internet, online hosting, Xbox, Microsoft, Apple, Steam or anything else) and collect their bills month by month.
- Upload the provider’s PDF: the app tries to read the total, consumption, unit price and due date; anything it cannot read you type into the same form.
- Share a utility with an invite link, a QR code or directly with people from your DevQuake referrals. Only the people on a utility can see its bills.
- “Individual meter required”: everyone sends a photo of their meter with the index for every bill; the app tries to read the index from the photo.
- Fair split: consumption × unit price for each person, with anything the meters do not cover shared equally; without meters the bill is split equally.
- The manager records what each person paid (cash, card or other); paying more or less is carried over to the next bill. Paid bills get a green check mark, others a warning.
- Comments on every bill, a month and year calendar of your own part, and statistics on consumption, payments and prices per category.
- Your name and address in your profile, shown only to the people you share a utility with.
